title: Design system maintenance & governance: contribution + review + deprecation workflow
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Create a unified governance document that defines: contribution guidelines for tokens and components (buttons, tables, charts), an explicit review checklist for design/engineering reviewers, a lightweight RFC path for API or token changes, and a deprecation policy with timelines and migration tooling recommendations.
background: Our design system has grown organically across product and platform teams. Recent merges changed token names and button variants with inconsistent migration notes, causing regressions in Console and Dedicated UI. We need a single source of governance that reduces breakage, speeds reviews, and standardizes deprecation procedures.
goals: 1) Reduce post-merge regressions caused by token/component changes. 2) Shorten review turnaround by providing a clear checklist and templates. 3) Provide a predictable deprecation timeline and tooling to migrate downstream apps. 4) Capture rules for semantic tokens, component props, and chart variants to enable safe automatic refactors.
out_of_scope: Refactoring every component in the library (separate initiative). Backend API versioning and release pipeline changes outside design artifacts.
design_guidelines_summary: - Tokens: prefer semantic names (eg. color-bg-primary) over raw hex names; group by intent not location. - Buttons: expose a limited variant set (primary, secondary, ghost, icon) and map legacy variants to new props via migration adapters. - Tables: single source of truth for row density tokens and accessibility text sizes. - Charts: standardized palette tokens and recommended small/large variants; document default axis styles and micro-interaction timings.
semantic_token_rules: Always define token with 'purpose-modifier' pattern (eg. 'bg-surface-elev-1', 'text-action-muted'). Include a canonical alias list for legacy names. New tokens must include: description, intended scope (global/component/local), accessibility notes (contrast ratio), and a suggested migration mapping.
rfc_process: Lightweight RFC required for changes that add, rename, or remove tokens or component props. RFC checklist: motivation, API surface change, migration plan, compatibility impact, perf considerations, screenshots, and rollout strategy. RFC review window: minimum 5 business days. RFC author must list at least one design and one engineering reviewer. RFC template stored: https://confluence.redwood.com/ds-rfcs/template
review_checklist: Is the change driven by a clear user or product need?
Does the token/component change include accessibility checks (WCAG 2.1 AA contrast)?
Are migration mappings or deprecation shims provided for downstream consumers?
Does the change introduce new runtime cost or render-path complexity? (e.g., dynamic style calc in hot path)
Have visual regression screenshots been produced for all supported themes and breakpoints?
Are unit and integration tests added for component behavior and token usage?
Is documentation updated (Storybook, tokens catalog, migration guide)?
Has the release and rollout cadence been defined (canary windows, dark launches)?
Has the change owner identified impacted repos/apps and notified them?
deprecation_policy_summary: Deprecation phases: Notice -> Soft-deprecate -> Remove. Standard timeline: 8 weeks notice + 4 weeks soft-deprecation (compat shims enabled) + removal on next major release (minimum 12 weeks total). For tokens used across >3 repos or any runtime change affecting Dedicated/Private customers, extend notice to 12 weeks and coordinate with account success.
migration_and_tooling_recommendations: - Provide codemods for common renames (JSCodeshift/ts-morph) and example scripts. - Add a 'compat' layer in the design system package that maps legacy tokens to new tokens behind a feature flag. - Provide a CLI report that scans repos for legacy token usage and outputs top consumers. - Add Storybook examples demonstrating old vs new usage and recommended fixes.
rollback_and_fallback: Every breaking change must include a rollback plan: a reversible PR that re-enables old tokens or a feature-flagged toggle. In incidents, rollback should be possible within one release window. Document responsible on-call and escalation path in the RFC.
communication_plan: - Publish RFC in Confluence and tag #design-system Slack channel. - Open a lightweight announcement doc for engineering and product with migration steps and a rough calendar. - Notify customer-facing teams when consumer impact is medium/high; coordinate blog or release notes for major removals.
release_and_rollout: - Small non-breaking changes: merged to main, automatic patch release. - Token renames or prop removals: gated behind feature flag, staged canary (10% of traffic) for 2 weeks, then gradual rollout. - Official removal only after deprecation window completes and codemods are available.
owner_and_stewardship: Design team maintains tokens, component library maintainers own components. Each change must list an explicit steward (design author and eng owner). Steward rotation: quarterly review of active token set.
acceptance_criteria: - Governance doc published in Confluence and linked from DS README. - RFC template populated in Confluence and validated by at least one RFC submission. - Codemod proof-of-concept for one token rename. - Checklist added to PR template for DS repo. - Stakeholder approval from Platform Eng and PM.

notes_and_tradeoffs: Trade-off: stricter governance will slow ad-hoc component changes but reduces production regressions. Trade-off: providing compat shims increases maintenance surface but improves consumer upgrade experience. Decided to require RFC for any token rename that affects >1 repo. Small visual-only tokens can follow an expedited 2-week notice.
